source_documents.title: OK
source_documents.content_text: OK (also spelled okay, ok, or O.K.) is an English word denoting approval, acceptance, agreement, assent, acknowledgment, or a sign of indifference. OK is frequently used as a loanword in other languages. The origins of the word are disputed, but the most widely accepted theory traces it to an 1839 abbreviation of 'oll korrect', a humorous misspelling of 'all correct', which was part of a broader fad of abbreviations in Boston newspapers during the late 1830s. Allen Walker Read, a Columbia University etymologist, published a series of articles in 1963-1964 establishing this origin.

source_documents.title: TIL the word 'OK' originated as a joke abbreviation in an 1839 Boston newspaper
source_documents.content_text: The Boston Morning Post published it on March 23, 1839. It was part of a fad where people would abbreviate misspelled phrases. Other examples from the same era include KY for 'know yuse' (no use) and KG for 'know go' (no go). OK is the only one that survived.

core_facts: OK first appeared in print on March 23, 1839, in the Boston Morning Post
It stood for 'oll korrect', a humorous misspelling of 'all correct'
It was part of a fad of abbreviating misspelled phrases in 1830s Boston newspapers
Allen Walker Read (Columbia University) established this origin in the 1960s
OK is now used as a loanword in virtually every language on Earth
Other abbreviations from the same fad (KY, KG, OW) all died out — only OK survived
surprising_angles: The most universally understood word on Earth was invented as a joke
OK survived while every other abbreviation from the same fad died
Telegraph operators adopted OK because it was fast to tap in Morse code
common_misconceptions: OK does NOT come from the German 'Ober-Kommando'
OK does NOT come from a Haitian port 'Aux Cayes' famous for rum
OK does NOT come from a railroad freight agent named Obadiah Kelly
summary.best_hook_material: The most used word on Earth was invented as a newspaper joke in 1839
summary.confidence_notes: Allen Walker Read's research is widely accepted. The 'oll korrect' origin is the scholarly consensus.
